newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amaprop rises on refocusing news.
newsitem.headline: Amaprop rises on refocusing news.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Anglo American Properties Ltd (Amaprop) rose on Tuesday on news the firm is to refocus its portfolio away from direct real estate property ownership and towards investing in property firms.
The firm's shares jumped 35 cents, or more than ten percent, to 305 cents by 1225 GMT.
"The anouncement is seen as a positive factor," one dealer said.
South African holding firm Anglo American Property Services Ltd (Ampros) said Amaprop would change its focus from direct ownership to investment in listed and unlisted property vehicles.

"Amaprop will effectively be stripped of all its direct property investments in a bid to realise the underlying value of this portfolio, as the share has been trading at a substantial discount to net asset value," said Ampros managing director Gerald Leissner said in a statement.
The news was part of a wider Ampros strategy shift in its operations that will see the firm distance itself away from city centre properties.
Ampros plans to sell 300 million rands worth of city centre properties as part of a restructuring of three of its listed units.
The firms involved in the rejig are Apex Property Fund, Compass Property Holdings and Amaprop. A fourth listed unit, Main Street Property, will continue with its present focus.

"The objective of the disposals is to accelerate Apex's strategy to become a decentralised office fund, to bring greater focus to Compass and to restructure Amaprop's portfolio to exclude direct property investments," Leissner said.
Apex was up one cent to 68 cents, Compass was unchanged at 134 cents and Main Street was also unmoved at 154 cents.
